stateLegislativeUncontestedShare.citation: Share of state legislative seats with no major-party competition in the general election: 38 percent in 2024 (2,227 of 5,807 seats), 39 percent averaged over 2010 to 2024 (Ballotpedia, Annual State Legislative Competitiveness Report, Vol. 14, 2024; https://news.ballotpedia.org/2024/09/27/ballotpedia-releases-14th-annual-state-legislative-competitiveness-report/).

usHousePrimaryCandidatesPerSeat.citation: 1,773 candidates ran in 2024 U.S. House primaries, the fewest since 2016 (1,588 in 2016), over 435 seats (Ballotpedia, Annual Congressional Competitiveness Report, 2024; https://ballotpedia.org/Annual_Congressional_Competitiveness_Report,_2024). The per-seat division is ours. By state the average ran from 3.6 (Oklahoma) to 10.9 (Maryland) in 2024 (Ballotpedia state primary pages).
usHousePrimaryCandidatesPerSeat.estimatedFrom: Ballotpedia 2024 House primary counts over 435 seats; spread 3.6 to 7 by state

usHouseContestedByBothParties.citation: 91.3 percent of U.S. House races in 2024 were contested by both the Democratic and the Republican parties (Ballotpedia, Annual Congressional Competitiveness Report, 2024).

stateLegislativeOpenSeatShare.citation: 962 of the 5,807 state legislative seats up for election on November 5, 2024 were open, 16.6 percent (Ballotpedia, Annual State Legislative Competitiveness Report, Vol. 14, 2024; https://ballotpedia.org/Open_seats_in_state_legislative_elections,_2024). Open seats were at their second-lowest point in eight election cycles (Ballotpedia News, Aug. 21, 2024).

largestCitiesMayoralCandidatesPerElectio.citation: Cities among the 100 largest whose 2026 filing deadlines had passed averaged 5.7 mayoral candidates each, the third-lowest since 2020; the 2020 to 2025 average at that point in the year was 6.1 (Ballotpedia News, 'A look at competitiveness in the 2026 mayoral elections', April 15, 2026; https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/04/15/a-look-at-competitiveness-in-the-2026-mayoral-elections/).

allSeatsUncontestedShare2025.citation: An average of 29 percent of seats nationwide were uncontested in the 2025 general election, where a race is uncontested when the candidates who filed number no more than the seats on the ballot (Ballotpedia, Election results, 2025: Uncontested races by state; https://ballotpedia.org/Election_results,_2025:_Uncontested_races_by_state). 30 percent were uncontested in the 2020 general election (Ballotpedia News).

nobodyFilesRules.citation: No single multistate summary of what happens when nobody files was found. Examples: Washington strikes the office from the ballot and the incumbent holds over until a successor is elected (RCW 29A.24.201, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/RCW/RCW%20%2029A%20TITLE/RCW%20%2029A.%2024%20%20CHAPTER/RCW%20%2029A.%2024%20.201.htm); South Carolina holds the election and a write-in can win (Attorney General opinion, https://www.scag.gov/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/00148019.pdf); Illinois and Maine examples appoint or hold a special election (local news). The rule is state law, so the game reads it from place data (src/core2/data/offices/holdover.json), not from this number. Read from a search result's text, not the opened page (ballotpedia.org refused direct fetches from the session, Nov 8, 2026).
